title: Financial Stability Review
summary: This is the ECB Financial Stability Review landing page, not the full report itself. The November 2025 release page reports that financial stability vulnerabilities remain elevated due to uncertainty over geoeconomic trends and the impact of tariffs, and also examines systemic risks arising from linkages between banks and non-bank financial intermediaries. The next FSR release is scheduled for 27 May 2026.
key_points: The November 2025 FSR identifies financial stability vulnerabilities as elevated due to geoeconomic uncertainty and tariff impacts
The report examines systemic risk arising from bank-non-bank financial intermediary linkages
Press release, presentation slides by VP Luis de Guindos, and statistical data are available as supplementary materials
ECB Podcast episodes discuss AI, stablecoins, private markets, trade tensions, and cyber threats in the context of financial stability
Next Financial Stability Review release is scheduled for 27 May 2026
Historical releases available back to November 2023
why_it_matters: The ECB Financial Stability Review is a semi-annual assessment of risks to euro area financial stability. This record captures the official metadata and thematic summary from the ECB website for the November 2025 FSR release. Market participants monitor these reports to understand the ECB's assessment of systemic vulnerabilities. The elevated risk environment noted, driven by tariff uncertainty and geoeconomic trends, provides context for macro trading and risk management decisions. Note: The substantive report with specific data, figures, and analysis is contained in the FSR PDF and press release.
macro_context: The FSR landing page highlights elevated financial stability risks in the euro area driven by geoeconomic uncertainty and tariff impacts, which influence the ECB's broader policy calculus and risk assessment for the region.
